audit_findings.title: Recurring customer-financing investment may be missing from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $118.3m net 2025 increase; $40.8m net increase in H1 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring investment in contract assets, consideration paid to customers, lease receivables, and deferred commissions reduces OE and must also be funded during forecast growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash used to fund contract assets and consideration paid to customers arising from customer commitment arrangements also increased in 2025, compared to the prior year.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates substantial recurring customer-financing investment, but the supplied record does not demonstrate whether OE already deducts it. Contract assets increased $66.4m and consideration paid to customers increased $53.5m in 2025, partly offset by $1.0m and $0.6m declines in lease receivables and deferred commissions, respectively. The resulting $118.3m equals 11.1% of the $1,061.9m anchor. If wholly omitted, the base value would fall by approximately $27 per share and the buy-below level from $171.37 to about $152.47, making the unresolved possibility material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year to operating cash flow and the annual changes in all four customer-financing accounts. Determine what portion is already captured, establish a normalized reinvestment-to-revenue or placement ratio, and rerun all scenarios for any omitted amount.

audit_findings.title: Recurring capitalized software may be misclassified as growth capex
audit_findings.mechanism: Any recurring software development excluded from maintenance capex would increase the maintenance-capex deduction and reduce OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Software developed to deliver hosted services to our customers has been designated as internal-use, and we capitalize certain costs incurred in connection with developing or obtaining internal-use software.
audit_findings.explanation: The recurring expenditure is demonstrated, but its exclusion from maintenance capex is not. Even treating the entire $36.458m of 2025 capitalized internal-use software as an omitted maintenance requirement would equal only 3.4% of the $1,061.9m anchor and approximately $8.3 per base-value share. That scale would not change the valuation conclusion relative to the $535.38 market price, and the actual error would be smaller if any amount is already deducted or legitimately supports growth.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the maintenance-capex schedule to the property-and-equipment cash-flow detail, identify the software amount already included, and rerun only for the recurring portion excluded from the current deduction.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 tax benefit is above the disclosed forward run rate
audit_findings.mechanism: Using the unusually low 2025 tax burden in an after-tax OE anchor overstates recurring OE and every forecast cash flow grown from it.
audit_findings.evidence: This increase in the projected 2026 effective tax rate is primarily due to estimated reductions in share-based compensation tax benefits, as compared to 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed 2025 effective tax rate was 20.0%, while management projected approximately 21.3% for 2026 because share-based-compensation tax benefits were expected to decline. Applying the 1.3-point difference to 2025 pretax income of $1,324.189m produces an approximately $17.2m adjustment, only 1.6% of the OE anchor and roughly $3.9 per base-value share. This would not change the valuation conclusion relative to the market price.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate the anchor using a sustainable effective tax rate supported by management's outlook and subsequent filings, retain SBC expense, and rerun the scenarios to confirm the limited effect.

audit_findings.title: Net-investment hedge liabilities may be an omitted claim
audit_findings.mechanism: A net derivative liability not otherwise reflected would be deducted in the equity bridge, subject to any economic offset from the hedged foreign net assets.
audit_findings.evidence: The changes in fair value of the cross currency swap contracts are recorded in AOCI and will be reclassified to earnings when the foreign subsidiaries are sold or substantially liquidate d or all or a portion of the hedge no longer qualifies for hedge accounting treatment.
audit_findings.explanation: At June 30, 2026, cross-currency swaps had $9.558m of liabilities and $4.895m of assets, producing a $4.663m net liability. That is approximately $0.06 per diluted share and 0.02% of the $19.839bn base equity value. Even deducting the gross liability without offsets would be only about $0.12 per share, so the item cannot materially change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Document enforceable counterparty netting and the relationship to the foreign net assets. If the $4.663m net liability is not otherwise captured, deduct it in the bridge and confirm that no offset is counted twice.

audit_findings.title: A litigation reversal modestly benefits the anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The nonrecurring reduction of litigation expense increases 2025 earnings and OE unless removed from the anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: General and administrative expense decreased primarily due to a $61.5 million expense in the prior year and a reduction in accrued expense of approximately $9 million in the first quarter of the current year, related to a now-concluded litigation matter, partially offset by higher personnel-related and information technology and security costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The $9m reversal is a demonstrated nonrecurring 2025 benefit, although the supplied record does not establish whether the OE calculation already removed it. At the filed 20.0% effective tax rate, its after-tax effect is approximately $7.2m, or 0.7% of the anchor and roughly $1.6 per base-value share. This is not large enough to change the valuation conclusion. The separate $80m settlement payment was for an expense accrued in prior years and must not be deducted again if the anchor was normalized for that cash-flow timing.
audit_findings.action: Trace both the $9m reversal and the $80m settlement through the 2025 OE reconciliation; remove the approximately $7.2m after-tax benefit if present while reversing any duplicate settlement deduction, then rerun.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded pension deficit is outside the stated bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: Any accumulated pension deficit not funded through forecast OE is a claim ahead of common equity and belongs in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, our Swiss Plans had a net unfunded pension obligation of $ 5.4 million, with a fair value of plan assets of $ 20.7 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed Swiss-plan deficit was $5.4m, equal to approximately $0.07 per diluted share and 0.03% of the $19.839bn base equity value. Even a full bridge deduction would not materially affect the valuation conclusion. The June 2026 filing does not provide an updated deficit, so the current amount remains unresolved but cannot plausibly become material without a very large deterioration.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the latest funded-status measurement and expected contribution schedule, then deduct only the portion not already represented by pension expense or forecast cash contributions.
